summary: Completed backend + frontend validation for legal routing/content, inquiry consent-removal behavior, downloads/print, mobile layout, and telemetry snippet removal on public preview URL.
critical_code_review_comments: Legacy backend tests were stale against intentional product change: consent is optional input and must be excluded from persistence. Updated regression tests now verify true/false/omitted consent all return 201 and never store consent.
No app-owned analytics snippet found in source/build index.html, and no runtime requests observed to ap.emergent.sh, emergent-main.js, or posthog during tested flows.
Legal content/routing implementation is consistent with the described non-binding inquiry model and explicit contract-by-confirmation wording.
seed_data_creation: Created transient TEST_ inquiry records during pytest and one browser-submitted inquiry; cleaned test records from Mongo (including specified main-agent UUID).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop/mobile legal screenshots saved under /app/test_reports/artifacts/iteration_8. First Playwright run failed once due tester selector typo (legal-footer-agb vs legal-footer-terms), not an app defect; corrected in second run. All requested scope checks passed afterward.
rca of the issue: Observed failures were in outdated test expectations, not app behavior. Root cause: prior tests still asserted consent persistence/rejection despite intentional backend change to ignore consent for pre-contract inquiries. Mitigation: updated test suite assertions and added consent true/false/omitted regression coverage.
